translationRepairs: When the Qiang besieged Dashuncheng, deputy general Zhao Huaide fought hard; his men tried to buy their way out of punishment with silver. Commander Li Fugui wanted to punish them for the disorder in his ranks.

When the Qiang besieged Dashuncheng, deputy general Zhao Huaide fought hard; his men used silver to buy severed heads to claim battle credit. Commander Li Fugui wanted to punish them for the disorder in his ranks.
以銀買級 means buying enemy heads (級) with silver to claim merit, not buying off punishment.
At Yulin the relief troops never came; he was struck by an arrow in midstream and died at fifty-seven.
At Yulin the relief troops never came; he was struck by a stray arrow and died at fifty-seven.
中流矢 means hit by a stray arrow; there is no stream.
Controllers Han Cunbao and the tribal general Xi Yaojiao tried to stop him, but he would not listen.
Controller Han Cunbao and the tribal general Xiayao both tried to stop him, but he would not listen.
瞎藥 is the tribal general's name; 交止之 means "both tried to stop him", not part of the name.
Several days later ten thousand barbarians suddenly gathered; Qi went out with too few men and was defeated.
Several days later ten thousand barbarians suddenly gathered; Qi rashly sallied out and was defeated.
輕出 means sallied out rashly/carelessly, not with too few men.
When he reached Zhuyan, he heard that the Jin were attacking the capital and returned at once.
When he reached Zhuqian, he heard that the Jin were attacking the capital and returned at once.
朱遷 is romanized Zhuqian; Zhuyan is a misreading.
After the Weizhou commander had surrendered, the Jin tempted Yougong with flattering words and promised him promotion, but he refused. They then reviled and humiliated him further.
After the Weizhou commander had surrendered, the commander tempted Yougong with flattering words and promised him promotion, but he refused. They then reviled and humiliated him further.
The subject of 誘以甘言 is the surrendered Weizhou commander (渭帥), not the Jin.
Shujiao was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Daizhao of Qin.
Shujiao was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Dao of Qin.
秦悼王 is Prince Dao of Qin (posthumous name 悼); Daizhao is a misreading.
Xun Zhi, style name Huidao, was a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Daozhong of Qin.
Xun Zhi, style name Huidao, was a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Dao of Qin.
秦悼王 is Prince Dao of Qin; there is no zhong in the title.
During the Jianyan era, Shu Ping served as military commandant of Shaanzhou, advanced through the ranks to Grandee of Martial Feathers, and was subsequently promoted to prefect.
During the Jianyan era, Shu Ping served as military commandant of Shaanzhou, advanced through the ranks to Grandee of Martial Wing, and was subsequently promoted to vice-prefect.
武翼大夫 is rendered Grandee of Martial Wing elsewhere; 通守 is a vice-prefect, not a prefect.
Yu Zhi was the son of Shu Dong, heir to Prince Anding.
Yu Zhi was the son of Shu Dong, Commandery Prince of Anding.
安定郡王叔東 names Shu Dong himself as Commandery Prince of Anding.
The officer Liu Qi, a Military Gentleman, also died in the fighting.
The officer Liu Jie, a Gentleman for Military Classics, also died in the fighting.
玠 is read Jie; 武經郎 is Gentleman for Military Classics.

When the report reached court, Yu Zhi was posthumously granted the rank of Left Grand General of the Gate Guard and Qi that of Military Grandee; members of both their families received official appointments.

When the report reached court, Yu Zhi was posthumously granted the rank of Left Grand General of the Gate Guard and Jie that of Grandee for Military Classics; members of both their families received official appointments.
玠 is read Jie; 武經大夫 is Grandee for Military Classics.

At that time Lü Huiqing was commanding the Yan-Yan frontier. Cui went to see him dressed for war. Huiqing asked what brought him, and Cui replied, "A great man comes to seek a great man—what other business could there be?"

At that time Lü Huiqing was commanding the Fuyan frontier. Cui went to see him dressed for war. Huiqing asked what brought him, and Cui replied, "A great man comes to seek a great man—what other business could there be?"
He was recommended for appointment as Left-Rank Palace Attendant and Director-General of troops on the Yan-Yan Route, and rose through the ranks to Military Gentleman.
He was recommended for appointment as Left-Rank Palace Attendant and Director-General of troops on the Fuyan Route, and rose through the ranks to Military Gentleman.

When the report reached court, an edict posthumously granted Xun Zhi the rank of Gentleman for Dispersing Morals and appointment to the Secretariat Pavilion, with the posthumous title Loyal and Resolute; Ziren was granted Vice Director of the Palace Library; their sons were given official posts; and the local people built a shrine in their honor.

When the report reached court, an edict posthumously granted Xun Zhi the rank of Gentleman for Dispersing Morals and appointment to the Secretariat Pavilion, with the posthumous title Loyal and Resolute; Ziren was granted Gentleman for Comprehensive Duty; their sons were given official posts; and the local people built a shrine in their honor.
通直郎 is the rank Gentleman for Comprehensive Duty, not a library post.
In the first year of Jianyan the Jurchens invaded Hedong, and the defending official Xi Yi fled.
In the first year of Jianyan the Jurchens invaded Hezhong, and the defending official Xi Yi fled.

Zhonglian was then defense commissioner of Guizhou. Pacification Commissioner Fan Zhixu dispatched him to command the Hedong horse and foot forces, encamped at Hedong, and temporarily placed him in charge of prefectural affairs.

Zhonglian was then defense commissioner of Guizhou. Pacification Commissioner Fan Zhixu dispatched him to command the Hedong horse and foot forces, encamped at Hezhong, and temporarily placed him in charge of prefectural affairs.
屯河中 is encamped at Hezhong.
He served as observation commissioner of Tongzhou and deputy commander-in-chief of the Xijing horse and foot forces.
He served as observation commissioner of Tongzhou and deputy commander-in-chief of the Xihe horse and foot forces.
Han Qing was sixth commander of the Xijing horse and foot forces. He traveled secretly with Weifu, was captured by the Jurchens, and also cursed without cease until he died.
Han Qing was sixth commander of the Xihe horse and foot forces. He traveled secretly with Weifu, was captured by the Jurchens, and also cursed without cease until he died.
The Jurchens combined forces and entered the Yan-Yan region. Wang Shu himself blocked the route from Yanzhou and dispatched Controller Pang Shicai to block the route from Yan'an.
The Jurchens combined forces and entered the Fuyan region. Wang Shu himself blocked the route from Fuzhou and dispatched Controller Pang Shicai to block the route from Yan'an.
鄜延 is Fuyan; 鄜州 is Fuzhou.
There was also Gao Ziru of Dizhou.
There was also Gao Ziru of Didao.
Because Xijing Commander Liu Fa was defeated in battle on the Jingyuan Route he was demoted and suspended from office, but soon he was restored.
Because Xihe Commander Liu Fa was defeated in battle on the Jingyuan Route he was demoted and suspended from office, but soon he was restored.
Xing instructed general Peng Zhi in strategy: set an ambush at Jingshou; when the enemy arrived feign retreat. The Jin host indeed pursued Zhi, the ambush sprang, and the Jin commander was captured.
Xing instructed general Peng Qi in strategy: set an ambush at Jingshou; when the enemy arrived feign retreat. The Jin host indeed pursued Qi, the ambush sprang, and the Jin commander was captured.
彭玘 is read Peng Qi.
There was also Sun Anda, a Grandee of Martial Eminence, who served as military controller of Yingtian Prefecture.
There was also Sun Andao, a Grandee of Martial Eminence, who served as military controller of Yingtian Prefecture.
